sources.entry: GlusterFS | Scale-out network-attached storage file system

summary.one_liner: GlusterFS is a software-defined distributed storage system that scales to several petabytes and provides object, block and file interfaces.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Gluster as software-defined distributed storage that can scale to several petabytes, with interfaces for object, block and file storage. It points to external Gluster docs for documentation and to a Contributors guide for development workflow. Build and install instructions are said to be in an INSTALL file in the source tree. The source includes functional tests under tests/, run with ./run-tests.sh or individually via bash or prove, and each submitted patch is tested against them. A MAINTAINERS file lists the project maintainers.
use_cases: testing storage patches against the GlusterFS test suite
how_to_run: See the INSTALL file in the source tree for build and install instructions
Run the full functional test suite with ./run-tests.sh (only on a test machine, not production)
notable: Provides object, block and file storage from one software-defined system
Scales to several petabytes according to the README
Every submitted patch is tested by the functional .t test suite
Dual licensed under GPLv2 and LGPLv3+
caveats: The README gives only brief build instructions and defers details to an INSTALL file and external docs
The test script warns it kills all gluster processes, so it must not run on a machine with production GlusterFS
